Unit


                     there is A modal verb in the original statement, suggestion, etc., it sometimes changes when we
               report what was said or thought. The changes are summarised here:

                     modal verb in original             modal verb in report
                 B | could, would, should, might,       could, would, should, might,
                              ought to, used to,        needn't, ought to, used to, (i.e. no change) @-©
                     could have, should have, etc.      could have, should have, etc.
                 C | will, can, may                         would, could, might @  & @
                                                            will, can, may (existing or future situations and
                                                        present tense verb in reporting clause) @
                                                                or would, can or could, may or might
                                                        (existing or future situations and past tense verb in
                                                        reporting clause) @
                 D | shall                                  would  (talking about the future) @
                                                            should (offers, requests for advice, etc.) @
                 E | must                               must  or had to @
                     must  (= conclude; see Unit 18B)   must  @
                                                                 @

 Ee)               ©           meet you at the airport.’ > He said that he could meet us at the airport. @
                   ©)  ‘We might  drop in if we have time.’ > They said they might drop in if they have time. @
                    )  ‘You should have contacted me  earlier.’ She said | should have contacted her earlier. ©
                   ©   ‘She may have already left.’ + He thought she might have already left. @
                If the situation we are reporting still exists or is still in the future and the verb in the reporting clause
               has a present tense, we use will, can, and may in the reported clause (see Unit 32). Compare:
                   ©)  ‘Careful! You’ll fall through the ice!’ > | warned him he would fall through the ice. @ and
                   ©)      be in Paris at Christmas.’ > She tells me   be in Paris at Christmas. @
                If the situation we are reporting still exists or is still in the future and the verb in the reporting clause
                has a past tense, we can use either would or will, can or could, or may or might in the reported
               clause:
                   ©)  ‘The problem can be solved.’  They said the problem can / could be solved. @

                       ‘| shall    call you on Monday.’ — She told me she would call me on Monday. @
                       ‘Where shall | put this box?’ + He asked where he should put the box. ©

                       ‘You must  be home by 9 o'clock.’ > She said | must / had to be home by 9      @
                       (had to is more natural in speech)
                       ‘| didn’t hear the phone. | must be going deaf.’ — Alex thought he must be going deaf. @
                       ‘You mustn’t tell my brother.’  He warned me  that | mustn’t tell his brother. @

                Note that we sometimes  use a modal verb in a reported sentence when there is no modal verb in the
                original:
                   ()         not allowed to smoke here.’ — She told me that | mustn’t smoke there.
                       ‘My advice is to look for a new job now.’ > She said that | should look for a new job now.
